title: Miniature journey stitching lab
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal brainstorming scratchpad for a small, composable journey primitive idea — "Petals" — to stitch tiny conversational fragments into reusable, low-cost microjourneys that apps can assemble at runtime. Goal is: reduce repeated prompt/context costs, simplify UX composition, and enable progressive fidelity rollouts.

High-level idea (one-liner):
- Define tiny, self-contained conversation fragments (petals) with minimal context footprints and soft-state connectors; apps compose petals into a runtime journey graph that the runtime can stitch, cache, and rehydrate across requests.

Why? (hypotheses)
- Many product flows reuse 2–6 short turns (e.g., clarify -> small read -> short suggestion). Reusing canonical fragments cuts tokens and improves stability.
- Petals let product teams iterate on pieces independently and A/B at fragment granularity.
- Runtime can apply lower-fidelity models for common petals and higher fidelity for final summarization, saving cost.

Core primitives (rough):
- Petal (id): prompt-template + output-schema + token-budget-hint + metadata (version, owner).
- Connector: mapping between petal outputs and next-petal inputs (field names, optional transforms).
- Stitch: runtime operation to compile sequence of petals into a single execution plan with optional intermediate caching.
- Snapshot key: lightweight representation to rehydrate a petal's KV cache without replaying full prior context.

User stories (raw):
- As a product engineer, I want to assemble a welcome flow from existing petals so I can ship quicker and keep tokens low.
- As an SRE, I want to route low-cost petals to cheaper model tiers automatically.
- As an analyst, I want telemetry per-petal (latency, tokens, failure rate) to detect regressions.

Acceptance criteria (first pass):
- Define petal schema and store a minimum of 5 sample petals in a proto registry.
- Runtime can execute a 3-petal flow in one user request, applying caching where a petal appears twice.
- Telemetry emits per-petal token counts and end-to-end token delta vs naive monolithic prompt.

Success metrics (pilot):
- Token reduction >= 25% for composed flows vs monolithic prompt baseline.
- Median latency increase <= 10% when adding stitching overhead.
- Number of journeys built from petals >= 3 internal product tests.

Experiment matrix (quick):
- Model routing: all-petal high-quality vs hybrid (low-cost for intermediate petals). Measure cost and quality on 1000 sample flows.
- Caching strategies: no-caching vs per-petal prefix cache vs snapshot rehydrate. Measure token savings and hit-rate.
- Fallback behavior: if an intermediate petal fails, skip/pivot to fallback petal; measure UX loss and failure recovery.

Prototype API sketch (pseudo):
- POST /v1/petals/compose
  body: {"petal_ids": ["clarify-v1","fetch-facts-v2","summarize-v1"], "user_vars": {...}, "stitch_policy": "hybrid"}
- Response: stream of per-petal events + final structured output + token_breakdown

Operational considerations:
- Petal registry: access control, versioning, descriptor validation.
- Rollouts: per-petal canary — safe to flip single petal to new model/quantization.
- Security: ensure petal prompts don't leak customer data when reused across tenants (namespacing).

Open questions / risks:
- How to handle long-running 'stateful' petals that need deeper KV caches? (snapshotting vs replay).
- UX surface for product teams to debug composed journeys (replay tooling, per-petal logs).
- Attribution: how to charge customers for token counts that come from shared cached petals? per-tenant accounting required.
- Complexity tradeoff: extra orchestration vs direct prompt simplicity — where is the breakpoint?

Next steps (concrete):
1) Wireframe a tiny petal registry UI in FigJam (Mika).
2) Implement a minimal petal proto and 3-sample petals (Omar) — clarify, short-fact-fetch, micro-summary.
3) Create a sandbox runner: (local dev) take petal list and run against hosted models with caching toggles.
4) Run small internal experiment with Conversations team on onboarding flow, collect token + quality signals.

Notes to self (brainstorm fragments):
- Petal-level evals: bake small eval sets (gold outputs) for each petal to detect regressions.
- Consider a 'petal pack' marketplace: curated fragment bundles for common verticals (support, sales).
- Make connectors expressive: allow regex/JS small transforms for mapping outputs to next petal inputs — but restrict for safety.

Quick links / reminders:
- Related: CONFLUENCE-7632 (microjourney patterns).
- Follow up w/ infra: how feasible is snapshot rehydrate vs prefix caching in current runtime? (ask @infra).

Rough timeline (alpha): 6 weeks to proto + sandbox, 8–12 weeks for internal pilot if infra runway available.

End of scratchpad — will convert to a PRD outline after prototype results and a quick design session.
